words: فَمِنْهُم مَّنْ هَدَى ٱللَّهُ وَمِنْهُم مَّنْ حَقَّتْ عَلَيْهِ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says citing those God guided first provides evidence for the following statement that misguidance has become due for others.
rows.anchor: ذكر فعل الهداية أولا دليلا على فعل الضلال ثانيا دليلا على حقوق الهداية أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the decisive proof accessible to insight, the address turns to the audience because only sensory evidence remains to persuade them.
rows.anchor: ثم التفت إلى مخاطبتهم إشارة إلى أنه لم يبق بعد هذا الدليل القطعي في نظر البصيرة إلا الدليل المحسوس للبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those doubting the messengers are told to travel through the earth and inspect the dwellings and traces of past rejecters.
rows.anchor: أي فإن كنتم أيها المخاطبون في شك من إخبار الرسل فسيروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The audience should look at the dwellings and remains of those who denied the messengers after passing through their lands.
rows.anchor: إذا سرتم ومررتم بديار المكذبين وآثارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ signals immediate succession, fitting an urgent proof that should pull people from error; compare the slower ثم in 6:11.
rows.anchor: وعبر هنا بالفاء المشيرة إلى التعقب دون تراخ لأن المقام للاستدلال المنقذ من الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative presents the rejecters’ fate as something people ought to ask about and learn from.
rows.anchor: وأشار بالاستفهام إلى أن أحوالهم مما يجب أن يسأل عنه للاتعاظ به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejecters include ʿĀd and later peoples whose stories reached the audience from disbelieving ancestors whom they imitated.
rows.anchor: من عاد ومن بعدهم الذين تلقيتم أخبارهم عمن قلدتموهم في الكفرمن أسلافكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They chose to disobey the messengers, although this occurred within God’s will; their chosen violation of His command made the proof stand against them by ordinary human standards.
rows.anchor: فأوقعت بهم لأنهم خالفوا أمري باختيارهم مع جهلهم بإرادتي

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans read يهدي actively, indicating that God creates guidance in the heart.
rows.anchor: هذا على قراءة الكوفيين بفتح الياء وكسر الدال

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the verb in the passive: no one can guide a person whom God has judged astray, since none overcomes His command.
rows.anchor: على قراءة الجمهور بالبناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rare reading takes the verb from ḍalla, meaning to forget: one whom God has left without guidance is like someone forgotten.
rows.anchor: وقرئ شاذا بفتح الياء من ضل بمعنى نسي

rows.speaker: الصغاني
rows.claim: Al-Ṣaghānī records Arabic usage in which ḍalla a camel means that someone led the camel astray.
rows.anchor: ونقل الصغاني في مجمع البحرين أنه يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Arabs, dalāl is taking a path other than the straight course; here God causes the misdirected course, so the Prophet should not grieve over their failure to respond or suspect a flaw in his supplication, since his duty is only to convey.
rows.anchor: والضلال عند العرب سلوك غير سبيل القصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s intense desire for their guidance does not make their rejection a defect in his sincere counsel or prayer; his responsibility is to convey.
rows.anchor: فلا تحزن ولا يضيق صدرك من عدم تأثرهم بنصحك وإخلاصك في الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those God leaves astray will have no supporters to save them from the punishment that overtook earlier rejecters.
rows.anchor: أي ينصروكم عند مجازاتهم على الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement rebukes them and challenges them to prove their claim, enlist helpers to return them to truth if they cannot prove it, or avert their punishment.
rows.anchor: وتبكيت لهم وتقريع وحث وتهييج على أن يقوموا بأنفسهم ويستعينوا بمن شاؤوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After evidence of God’s power, knowledge, and wisdom in creation, their denial of resurrection continues the earlier pattern of rejecting messengers and invites astonishment.
rows.anchor: بعد قيام الأدلة على كمال قدرته وشمول علمه وبلوغ حكمته في إبداع جميع المخلوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They swear with utmost force that God will not raise the dead, basing their denial only on the fact that resurrection is unfamiliar to their experience.
rows.anchor: جعلت الأيمان جاهدة لكثرة ما بالغوا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their appeal to custom is irrational: the first creation also had no precedent, despite their claim to be exceptionally intelligent.
rows.anchor: استنادا منهم إلى مجرد استبعاد مالم تجر به نفسه عندهم عادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers that He will raise them: nothing prevents Him, He has promised it, can do it, and does not break His word.
rows.anchor: أي ليبعثهم لأنه لا مانع له من ذلك وقد وعد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people cannot reach knowledge of the unseen through unaided reason, which is confined to the visible world, and reject the divinely supported guides who convey it.
rows.anchor: لا علم لهم يوصلهم إلى ذلك لأنه من عالم الغيب لا يمكن عقولهم الوصول إليه بغير إرشاد من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People resist accepting what intellect alone cannot reach and then argue vehemently despite lacking access to the unseen.
rows.anchor: فلذلك ترى الإنسان منهم يأبى ذلك استعبادا لأن يكون شيء معقول لا يصل إليه بمجرد عقله وهو خصيم مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After two examples established God’s complete knowledge and power, this statement elaborates the preceding declaration that God knows, applying it to the unseen and the Hour.
rows.anchor: الدالان على تمام علمه وشمول قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone owns the unseen of the heavens and earth, just as He alone owns what is manifest, and can enact whatever He wills.
rows.anchor: هذاعلم الله في المشاهدات الذي علم من هذه الأدلة

words: وَمَآ أَمْرُ ٱلسَّاعَةِ إِلَّا كَلَمْحِ ٱلْبَصَرِ أَوْ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour’s coming is like a blink or nearer: by human reckoning its suddenness is immense, and people will rise quickly to the caller.
rows.anchor: أي كرجع الطرف المنسوب إلى البصر أي بصر كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Relative to God, the Hour’s majesty, speed, and precision exceed description and are certain; this follows because God can do every possible thing.
rows.anchor: وأما بالنسبة إليه سبحانه فأمره في الجلالة والعظم والسرعة والإتقان يجل عن الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After rebuking their false belief and ending with the Hour, the discourse turns to first creation as evidence of the Hour and of God’s power to act by choice.
rows.anchor: ولما انتقضى توبيخهم على إيمانهم بالباطل وكفرانهم بالحق

words: أَخْرَجَكُم مِّنۢ بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brought people from their mothers’ wombs knowing nothing, great or small; the One who did this can bring them from the earth even more readily.
rows.anchor: والذي أخرجكم منها قادر على إخراجكم من بطن الأرض بلا فرق بل بطريق الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing, sight, and hearts are faculties for removing the ignorance present at birth; God formed them in the inaccessible womb, so recreating people is easier still.
rows.anchor: آلات لإزالة الجهل الذي وقعت الولادة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī suggests hearing is singular while sight and hearts are plural because variation in them is greater, though only God knows its full extent.
rows.anchor: لأن التفاوت فيهما أكثر من التفاوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afʾida are hearts prepared to understand and regulate the body through the subtle heat within them, which can receive delicate meanings.
rows.anchor: والأفئدة هي القلوب التي هيأها للفهم وإصلاح البدن بما أودعها من الحرارة اللطيفة القابلة للمعاني الدقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faculties may bring people to gratitude when they hear admonitions and see signs, recognize God’s knowledge, power, and care, and acknowledge what His messengers conveyed.
rows.anchor: بمعارف القلوب التي وهبكموها إذا سمعتم المواعظ وأبصرتم الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chief lesson is that the benefactor is one God, all-knowing, all-powerful, and freely acting; natural forces are created and act only as He directs them.
rows.anchor: المنعم عليكم بهذه النعم إله واحد عالم بكل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ between direct address and third person because this context can address either the attentive or the turning-away audience; al-Mulk’s context addresses only the latter, so readers agree there.
rows.anchor: على اختلاف القراءتين لأن سياق الكلام وسباقه يحتمل المقبل والمعرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has subjected birds to flight in the air through the benefits and wisdom He placed in flight, abilities humans cannot match despite superior intellect.
rows.anchor: مذللات للطيران بما أقامهن الله فيه من المصالح والحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God keeps birds aloft; since humans and birds share nature, nature alone cannot explain their different abilities, answering philosophers who appeal to natural causes.
rows.anchor: لأن نسبتكم وإياها إلى الطبيعة واحدة

words: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extraordinary creation and subjection of birds are signs for people whom God has prepared to believe.
rows.anchor: أي الأمر العظيم من إخراجكم على تلك الهيئة

none: Qurʾān text and page markers only; no commentary in this segment.

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr transmits from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. al-Qāsim that Mālik defines hashing as shaking leaves and fruit from a branch with a hooked staff without breaking or beating it.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن القاسم عن الإمام مالك

rows.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
rows.claim: Maymūn b. Mihrān gives the same explanation of gently shaking foliage from branches.
rows.anchor: وكذا قال ميمون بن مهران

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the root sense of this word is softness, as in describing a man as هش.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : والأصل في هذه المادة الرخاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses cuts short his account out of respect for the King and eagerness to hear God speak, recalling the maxim against overfamiliarity on a royal carpet.
rows.anchor: خاف التطويل على الملك فقطع على نفسه ما هو فيه من لذة المخاطبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʾārib means needs or benefits, which perceptive people can understand.
rows.anchor: أي حوائج ومنافع يفهمها الألباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because maʾārib is a nonrational broken plural, it takes the feminine singular modifier أخرى; Moses leaves the particular uses unspecified.
rows.anchor: كان الأنسب معاملته معاملة الواحدة المؤنثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to cast down the staff, and Moses immediately obeys without hesitation.
rows.anchor: { قال ألقها } أي العصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic word ḥayya applies to males and females and creatures of any size; its huge final form is called thuʿbān, while quick movement earns the name jān.
rows.anchor: والحية اسم جنس يقع على الذكر والأنثى والصغير والكبير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the staff became a yellow serpent with a horse-like crest and swelled until it became a thuʿbān.
rows.anchor: فعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنها صارت حية صفراء لها عرف كعرف الفرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transformed staff was enormous like a thuʿbān and swift like a jān.
rows.anchor: فهي في عظم الثعبان وسرعة الجان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses naturally feared the serpent, and God’s command to take it was training him for what he would face before Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: اي الله تبارك وتعالى على ما يكون منها عند فرعون لأجل التدريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sīra means way or state; God promises to restore the serpent to its former state as a staff, a promise that cannot fail.
rows.anchor: أي بعظمتنا عند أخذك لها بوعد لا خلف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign confirms that the speaker is the Lord with the most beautiful names; Moses becomes calm, puts his hand in the serpent’s mouth, takes its beard, and finds his hand between the staff’s prongs.
rows.anchor: وبلغ من طمأنينته أن أدخل يده في فمها وأخذ بلحيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here janāḥ means the side beneath the upper arm; in al-Qaṣaṣ it refers to the hand, with the nearby place named for what occupies it.
rows.anchor: والأبط , والجانب - قاله في القاموس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hand emerges brilliantly white, like the sun, while retaining its original color and without leprosy or any other illness.
rows.anchor: أي مرض لا برص ولا غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī avoids naming leprosy because Arabs disliked hearing its name; denying the broader category of illness is stronger than denying leprosy alone.
rows.anchor: ولما كان البرص أبغض شيء إلى العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transformed staff and illuminated hand are another sign, among God’s greatest signs, shown to steady Moses’ heart and increase his certainty.
rows.anchor: افعل ما أمرتك به من إلقاء العصا وضم اليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is sent to turn Pharaoh back from rebellion; Pharaoh exceeded the bounds of servanthood and claimed divinity.
rows.anchor: { اذهب إلى فرعون } أي لترده عن عتوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement of Pharaoh’s transgression is emphatic because anyone’s rebellion against the Supreme King is extraordinary.
rows.anchor: مما للملك الأعلى مما يستبعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks for an expanded heart because confronting Pharaoh is a grave task requiring great fortitude and composure.
rows.anchor: ما لا يحتمله إلا ذو جأش رابط وصدر فسيح قلب ضابط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses first leaves the object of expansion general, then specifies his chest, reinforcing the request generally and specifically.
rows.anchor: ولما أبهم المشروح ليكون الكلام أوكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks God to make his mission easy, clarifying the general request for an expanded heart.
rows.anchor: ثم بين ذلك الإبهام بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knot is a speech impediment that kept Moses from expressing every intended point, caused by the coal placed in his mouth before Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: أي مما فيه من الحبسة عن الإتيان بجميع المقاصد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The account that Moses’ impediment came from a coal placed in his mouth before Pharaoh is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: كما نقل عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks only for the speech needed to convey his message and be understood, not complete removal of his impediment.
rows.anchor: ولذلك اقتصر على قدر الحاجة فلم يطلب زوال الحبسة كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wazīr is a refuge and helper who carries part of Moses’ burden; Moses prefers family because he trusts their compassion.
rows.anchor: أي ملجأ يحمل عني بعض الثقل ويعاونني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses identifies Aaron as his brother and the family member most likely to give him full support.
rows.anchor: أي لأنه أجدر أهلي بتمام مناصرتي

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads both verbs as first-person imperfects, presenting God’s answer: I will strengthen my support through him and include him in my mission.
rows.anchor: وأجاب الدعاء في قراءة ابن عامر فقال

rows.speaker: القراء الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers pronounce the first verb with hamzat al-waṣl and the second with fatḥ, making both imperatives addressed to God as supplications.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الباقين بوصل الأول وفتح الثاني على أنهما أمران مسندين إلى الله تعالى على الدعاء

none: Qurʾān text and page markers only; no commentary in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated command is emphatic because the danger is so great that ordinary human nature scarcely accepts the certainty of the order.
rows.anchor: مؤكدا لنفس الذهاب لأنه لشدة الخطر لا يكاد طبع البشر يتحقق جزم الأمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reason for the mission is repeated for emphasis and to heighten wonder at Pharaoh’s lack of sense, and at those who follow him.
rows.anchor: من قلة عقله , فكيف بمن تبعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who command right should begin with the gentlest approach; gentle speech leaves Pharaoh no excuse or grounds for complaint.
rows.anchor: بما ينبغي لكل آمر بالمعروف من الأخذ بالأحسن فالأحسن والأسهل فالأسهلن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gentle speech may prompt Pharaoh to recall God’s care through his changing stages and recognize God as his Lord, turning from error to faith.
rows.anchor: ما مر له من تطوير الله له في أطوار مختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh may fear the consequences of their message, suspect it is true, and send the Children of Israel with Moses and Aaron.
rows.anchor: أو يصل غلى حال من يخاف عاقبة قولكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression of hope describes a state reasonably hoped for by the speakers; the Qur’an follows human expectations in dialogue, while God knows what will occur.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الترجي أن يكون حاله حال من يرجى منه ذلك

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Biqāʿī cites Sibawayh’s discussion of verbal nouns and names for the grammatical account of this expression of hope.
rows.anchor: قاله سيبويه في باب من النكرة يجري مجرى ما فيه الألف واللام من المصادر والأسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Pharaoh was extremely powerful, Moses and Aaron felt they could be destroyed unless God protected them.
rows.anchor: ولما كان فرعون في غاية الجبروت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added nūn intensifies their fear and complaint so that reassurance can answer their distress in proportion to it.
rows.anchor: بإظهار النونالثالثة إبلاغا في إظهار الشكوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yafruta means Pharaoh might hasten to punish them before they finish conveying the message, like someone leaping toward a thing.
rows.anchor: بالعقوبة قبل إتمام البلاغ عجلة من يطفر ويثب إلى الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also fear that Pharaoh will exceed his current arrogance and go further in transgression.
rows.anchor: فيتجاوز إلى أعظم مما هو فيه من الاستكبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s reassurance rests on His protection of His allies and destruction of His enemies; His presence is unlike kings who disappear when dispatching envoys.
rows.anchor: لا أغيب كما تغيب الملوك إذا أرسلو رسلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God affirms hearing and sight: nothing about either messenger or their enemy is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: لا يخفى علي شيء من حال رسولي ولا حال عدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God again emphasizes that they must go and speak to Pharaoh before giving them the words to say.
rows.anchor: تسبب عنه تعليمهما ما يقولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic dual wording signals their joint support; calling God Pharaoh’s Lord reduces Pharaoh to a servant and refutes his claim to divinity.
rows.anchor: ان فرعون ينكر ما تضمنه قولهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call God Pharaoh’s Lord because He raised and nurtured him after bringing him from nonexistence, showing Pharaoh is only one of His servants.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى تحقيره بأنه من جملة عبيد مرسلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask Pharaoh to release the Children of Israel so they can worship God, since no one else deserves worship.
rows.anchor: فإنه لا يستحق العبادة غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They forbid Pharaoh to torment the Israelites through forced labor and slaughter.
rows.anchor: بما تعذبهم به من الاستخدام والتذبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle introducing their sign anticipates the audience’s expectation that a claim of messengership be supported with evidence.
rows.anchor: مفتتحا بالحرف التوقع لأن حال السامع لادعاء الرسالة أن يتوقع دلالة على الإرسال

rows.speaker: الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Some philosophers who affirm God’s oneness deny that the spirit is a subtle body, force in a body, or bodily form; they describe its tie to the body as governance and action.
rows.anchor: وكان من الفلاسفة تناسخيتهم وغيرهم

rows.speaker: الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Some say that after leaving the body the spirit joins the intellectual world and angels; others connect it with a celestial body, and some who accept resurrection deny its return to its former body.
rows.anchor: وكان من الفلاسفة تناسخيتهم وغيرهم من يقر الله بالوحدانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronoun addresses the human being as body and soul together, answering theories that separate the soul’s fate from the body’s resurrection.
rows.anchor: الهيكل المجتمع من البدن والنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity was first created from earth through the creation of its father Adam, so the same earth can be the source of resurrection.
rows.anchor: في النشأة الأولى بخلق أبيكم آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At death body and soul return to earth and become dust; even if the spirit is in ʿIlliyyīn, it remains related to the body, which experiences its pleasure and pain.
rows.anchor: وللروح مع ذلك وأن كانت في عليين تعلق ببدنها بوجه ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says it is soundly established that a dead person sits in the grave and answers the two angels.
rows.anchor: وقد صح أن الميت يقعد في قبره ويجيب سؤال الملكين عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will bring people from earth at resurrection with the same power by which He created them at first, as He does with plants.
rows.anchor: يوم البعث بتلك العظمة بعينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation, death, and revival show that God alone acts by choice, not nature; whoever made life from what lacked life and returned it to lifeless earth can revive it, even more readily by ordinary analogy.
rows.anchor: كرة ردكم إلى ما كنتم عليه قبل الحياة ترابا لا روح فيه

words: مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَٰكُمْ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can escape the encompassing greatness and subtle wisdom by which God creates, returns, and raises people from earth.
rows.anchor: لا يقدر أحد منكم أن يخلص من تلك العظمة المحيطة بجليل عظمته ولا بدقيق حكمته
